claims.claim: Deere's Q3 2026 filing shows construction and forestry strength offsetting weakness in large production agriculture, while management said order-book trends reinforce 2026 as the bottom of the agricultural equipment cycle; this creates a possible cyclical inflection alongside continued advanced-technology adoption.

risks.risk: The claimed agricultural-cycle bottom is management's forward assessment and remains exposed to farm economics, tariffs and equipment inventory normalization.

unknowns.unknown: The timing and magnitude of a large-ag demand recovery are not established by one quarter of order-book improvement.

claims.claim: Deere reported Q3 2026 net income of $1.379B or $5.10/share versus $1.289B or $4.75/share a year earlier; worldwide net sales and revenues rose 5% to $12.608B, and full-year net-income guidance improved to $4.75B-$5.00B.

The 10-Q attributes quarterly improvement partly to favorable price realization, offset by higher production costs and unfavorable tax impacts, showing execution improvement with continuing cost pressure.

risks.risk: Large agriculture remains cyclically weak and higher material/production costs can pressure margins even as pricing helps.

unknowns.unknown: Whether improved orders convert into sustained 2027 production-agriculture revenue growth remains unknown.
